record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Disease-free global stability when R0<1<R in the vaccinated varying-population SEIRS case
record.original_question: For the varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS model with vaccination studied as the special case beta_e=0, e_r=0, gamma_r=0, gamma_s>=0, linear birth rate Lambda, and disease-induced death rate delta, let R0=s_dfe R where s_dfe=Lambda/(Lambda+gamma_s) and R is the corresponding reproduction factor without vaccination. In the regime R0<1<R, where the disease-free equilibrium is locally stable but R exceeds one, is the disease-free equilibrium globally asymptotically stable, and what Lyapunov function gives the most effective proof?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following compartmental epidemic model with susceptibles $s$, exposed $e$, infectious $i$, and removed $r$ compartments, governed by the ODE system

$$\begin{aligned}
 s' &= \Lambda - \beta_i\, s\, i - (\Lambda + \gamma_s)\, s + \gamma_r\, r,\\
 e' &= \beta_i\, s\, i - (\Lambda + \gamma_e)\, e,\\
 i' &= \gamma_e\, e - (\Lambda + \gamma + \delta)\, i,\\
 r' &= \gamma\, i + \gamma_s\, s - (\Lambda + \gamma_r)\, r,
\end{aligned}$$

with parameters $\Lambda>0$ (linear birth rate, also acting as natural death rate), $\beta_i>0$ (infection rate from $i$), $\gamma_e>0$ (progression rate from $e$ to $i$), $\gamma>0$ (recovery rate), $\delta\ge 0$ (disease-induced death rate), $\gamma_s\ge 0$ (vaccination rate of susceptibles), and $\gamma_r\ge 0$ (loss of immunity rate). Define
$$R = \frac{\beta_i\, \gamma_e}{(\Lambda+\gamma_e)(\Lambda+\gamma+\delta)}, \qquad s_{\rm dfe} = \frac{\Lambda}{\Lambda+\gamma_s}, \qquad R_0 = s_{\rm dfe}\, R.$$

The disease-free equilibrium (DFE) is the equilibrium with $e=i=0$. It is known to be locally asymptotically stable when $R_0<1$, and globally asymptotically stable when $R\le 1$ (via, e.g., the Lyapunov function $V(e,i)=\gamma_e\, e+(\gamma_e+\Lambda)\, i$).

Question: In the parameter regime $R_0<1<R$, is the disease-free equilibrium globally asymptotically stable on the biologically relevant invariant region? If so, exhibit a Lyapunov function (in the variables $s,e,i,r$) yielding the most effective proof of global asymptotic stability.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly identified as an open question in the surveyed literature on SIR-PH epidemic models with vaccination. A web check did not reveal a later paper establishing global asymptotic stability of the DFE in the gap regime $R_0<1<R$ for this varying-population SEIRS model with vaccination, nor a definitive "most performant" Lyapunov function. Status remains open to the best of available evidence.

status_evidence.title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models (arXiv:2205.03700)
status_evidence.snippet: Remark 3 ... This leaves open the case R0 < 1 < R, when the DFE is locally, but perhaps not globally stable, and also the question of choosing the 'most performant' Lyapunov function.
status_evidence.claim: The question of global asymptotic stability of the DFE in the regime R_0<1<R, and the choice of an optimal Lyapunov function, is stated as open.
